text_to_speech: A pipet is used to dispense a precise volume of liquid. It must be used together with a pipet bulb or pipet pump. Pipets take practice. Before using a pipet to obtain experimental data, you should practice a few times with water. This allows you to get a feel for how to use a pipet. First, squeeze the bulb to remove the air. Rest the bulb gently on top of the pipet. You do not need to jam the bulb on top; it simply rests against the pipet to make a seal. Release the bulb slowly to draw liquid into the pipet. Do not allow the liquid to splash up into the bulb. When you have drawn up enough liquid, replace the pipet bulb with your index finger or thumb. From this point on, use your finger to control the flow of liquid into the receiving container. Graduated pipets are marked every 0.1 mL, which means they can be used to measure liquid volumes to the hundredths place. Notice that the markings start at 0 at the top, and increase down the length of the pipet. To use a pipet, draw up slightly more liquid than you need to dispense. It’s not necessary to pull liquid all the way to the zero line. Remember, after drawing up enough liquid with the pipet bulb, you will use your finger to control the flow. Record your initial measurement to the hundredths place. Slowly release liquid into your receiving container until the desired amount has been dispensed. Record this final volume, to the hundredths place. The volume dispensed will be calculated by difference: the final volume minus the initial volume equals the volume dispensed.
